items.followUp: Why is the third ionization energy of magnesium higher than its second ionization energy?

rubric.why: The first ionization removes an electron from neutral magnesium and forms Mg⁺.
rubric.description: Identifies the ion from which the second electron is removed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the second electron is removed from Mg⁺.

rubric.why: The remaining electrons in the positive ion are attracted more strongly to the nucleus, so removing another electron requires more energy.
rubric.description: Explains why the second ionization energy is higher.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the electron is more strongly attracted to the nucleus or that more energy is required.

modelAnswer: The first ionization of magnesium removes one electron from a neutral Mg atom and forms Mg⁺.
The second electron is removed from Mg⁺ and is attracted more strongly to the nucleus; therefore, more energy is required.
Thus, the second ionization energy of magnesium is higher than the first.

items.followUp: Classify molecules according to the number of atoms they contain and give an example of each type.

rubric.why: These types of molecules are classified according to the number of atoms in each molecule.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that classification is based on the number of atoms in a molecule.

rubric.why: A monoatomic molecule contains one atom; a correct example is required.
rubric.description: Gives a monoatomic molecule and an example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct type-and-example pair.

rubric.why: A diatomic molecule contains two atoms; a correct example is required.
rubric.description: Gives a diatomic molecule and an example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct type-and-example pair.

rubric.why: A triatomic molecule contains three atoms; a correct example is required.
rubric.description: Gives a triatomic molecule and an example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct type-and-example pair.

rubric.why: A polyatomic molecule contains more than three atoms; a correct example is required.
rubric.description: Gives a polyatomic molecule and an example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct type-and-example pair.

modelAnswer: Molecules may be classified according to the number of atoms they contain.
A monoatomic molecule contains one atom; for example, He.
A diatomic molecule contains two atoms; for example, H₂.
A triatomic molecule contains three atoms; for example, H₂O.
A polyatomic molecule contains more than three atoms; for example, NH₃.

items.followUp: Define molecular formula and write the molecular and empirical formulae of glucose.

rubric.why: An empirical formula expresses the simplest whole-number ratio of the atoms of each element in a compound.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it gives the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms of each element.

rubric.why: The question requires two valid examples of empirical formulae.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any two valid examples, such as H₂O and CH₂O.

modelAnswer: An empirical formula shows the simplest whole-number ratio of the atoms of each element in a compound.
Examples are H₂O and CH₂O; CH₂O is the empirical formula of glucose, C₆H₁₂O₆.
